prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: Business software subscription pricing (language en).
Grid: 6 columns × 8 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Merged cells: "Plan" spans 1 col × 2 row; "Price" spans 2 col × 1 row; "Minimum seats" spans 1 col × 2 row; "Contract" spans 1 col × 2 row; "Support" spans 1 col × 2 row.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Plan" · longest unbreakable word 75px · one-line width 75px
  col 2: header "Price › List price" · longest unbreakable word 37px · one-line width 67px
  col 3: header "Price › Billing terms" · longest unbreakable word 86px · one-line width 490px
  col 4: header "Minimum seats" · longest unbreakable word 66px · one-line width 109px
  col 5: header "Contract" · longest unbreakable word 63px · one-line width 123px
  col 6: header "Support" · longest unbreakable word 79px · one-line width 195px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 707px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 706px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 707px (different strategies, not small variations).
Reply ONLY JSON: {"understanding":{"purpose":"","reading":"","groups":["columns that belong together and why"],"keep_intact":[""],"may_wrap":[""]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[int px per column, column 1 first],"idea":"one sentence"}]}

log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"A plan-comparison price sheet: the reader first identifies a plan, then reads across to see what it costs, what the billing commitment is, and what operational constraints (seats, contract, support) come with it.","reading":"Mostly row-wise: the eye anchors on the Plan name, jumps to the Price block (list price then the billing sentence that explains it), then continues right to the short fact columns (seats, contract, support) which are scanned vertically for comparison between plans. Column 3 is prose, not a value; columns 2/4/5/6 are short comparable facts.","groups":["cols 1 alone — row identity, the entry point for every scan","cols 2–3 — one merged 'Price' header; the number and its terms must be adjacent and read together","cols 4–6 — short constraint/support facts of equal role, read as a small comparable block","col 2 vs cols 4–6 — numeric/short tokens that benefit from tight, uniform widths"],"keep_intact":["Plan names, especially 'Enterprise' (75px, must not break)","'List price' and 'Billing terms' as word units (no mid-word breaks)","'Minimum seats', 'Contract', 'Support' as word units in the header","dollar amounts ($12, $45) and figures like 250+ in the billing text","'12-month', '40%' tokens inside billing text"],"may_wrap":["Billing terms sentence in col 3 (longest, 490px one-line — the natural place to absorb height)","'List price' header over two lines","'Minimum seats' header over two lines","Support descriptions in col 6","Contract wording in col 5"]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[96,58,281,87,84,100],"idea":"Billing-maximal: squeeze every short column to its word-safe minimum so the billing sentence gets 260px of text and wraps to only two lines, keeping the prose readable as a sentence."},{"name":"B","widths":[100,70,200,115,110,111],"idea":"Balanced grid: no column is starved — the price block still dominates but the three right-hand fact columns get comfortable, near-equal widths so seat, contract and support values stay scannable vertically."},{"name":"C","widths":[110,62,160,130,120,124],"idea":"Identity-and-facts-first: generous Plan column plus three wide comparable fact columns, with billing terms treated as a small paragraph that wraps to three or four lines beside them."}]}
